STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r6.claim: Moses kills an Egyptian quarreling with an Israelite, then flees Egypt for Midian.
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r6.anchor: striking and killing an Egyptian who was quarreling with an Israelite and the subsequent flight of Moses from Egypt to Midian (vv. 14–22)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r1.claim: بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ means reaching adolescence, while اسْتَوَى adds intellectual and temperamental balance; youth without poise is insufficient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r1.anchor: beauty of poise in sense and temperament

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r2.claim: حُكْم means decision-making power and عِلْم means comprehension of God; both have levels, and here they are not prophetic wisdom because Moses’ commission came later.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r2.anchor: because the incidents of the early life of Moses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r3.claim: مُحْسِنِينَ are people who use their abilities well and fully; God rewards such people with wisdom, while failure to attain it wastes their abilities and youth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p529/r3.anchor: people who use their abilities in the right way at the optimum level

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r1.claim: Moses was educated in the palace and received wisdom and knowledge from God upon reaching maturity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r1.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ sarayda iyi bir eğitim gördü. Olgunluk çağına ulaşınca Allah tarafından kendisine “hikmet ve ilim” verildi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r2.claim: Before his prophethood, Moses knew Pharaoh was wrong and saw Pharaoh oppressing the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r2.anchor: Mûsâ, kendisine daha peygamberlik gelmeden Firavun’un yanlış yolda olduğunu biliyor ve İsrâiloğulları’na baskı uyguladığını görüyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r3.claim: The author surmises that Moses disclosed his opposition to relatives, hid after it spread, and went into the city only at night.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r3.anchor: muhalefeti ağızdan ağıza yayılınca da gözden kaybolup kendini gizlemişti. Şehre ancak geceleri çıkıyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r4.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r4.claim: Most commentators identify the unnamed city as the Egyptian city where Pharaoh resided.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r4.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğuna göre Mısır’da Firavun’un ikamet ettiği şehirdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r5.speaker: Dahhâk
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r5.claim: Dahhak identifies the city as present-day Aynişems, once an independent settlement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r5.anchor: Müfessir Dahhâk buranın geçmişte müstakil bir yerleşim merkezi olan bugünkü Aynişems olduğunu söylemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r6.claim: Shawkani identifies the city as Cairo.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r7.claim: Some identify it as Memphis, the center of northern Egypt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:14/r7.anchor: Kuzey Mısır’ın merkezi Menfis olabileceğini söyleyenler de vardır

QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r3.claim: When Moses matured, God gave him judgment by completing his preparation and granting him knowledge; this is God’s way with the eminent and prophets.
QUSHAYRI:v2p431/r3.anchor: لما كملت سنه وتم عقله ، واستوى كمال خصاله

FARRA:v2p303#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r1.speaker: العقيلي
FARRA:v2p303#2/r1.claim: A line recited by al-ʿUqaylī treats the first occurrence of ʿām in the phrase year after year as redundant.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r2.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r2.claim: Sībawayh analyzes “al-ashudd” as the plural of “shiddah,” like niʿmah/anʿum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r2.anchor: جمع شدة كنعمة وأنعم، هذا قول سيبويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r3.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r3.claim: Another grammarian analyzes “al-ashudd” as the plural of “shadd.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r4.claim: A group treats “al-ashudd” as a singular noun rather than a plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة «الأشد» اسم مفرد وليس بجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r5.claim: One group sets the age of “al-ashudd” at puberty, around fifteen years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r5.anchor: فقالت فرقة: بلوغ الحلم وهي نحو خمسة عشر عاما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r6.claim: Another group sets the age at eighteen years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r7.claim: Al-Suddī gives twenty years as the age of maturity.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r10.speaker: مجاهد، ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r10.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the age of maturity as thirty-three years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن عباس: ثلاثة وثلاثون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r11.speaker: فرقة عظيمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r11.claim: A large group gives thirty-six years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r12.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r12.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say “istawā” means forty years.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r13.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r13.claim: Makki transmits a view that “istawā” means sixty years; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r13.anchor: وقال مكي وقيل هو ستون سنة وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r14.claim: “Al-ashudd” means bodily strength and firmness; “istawā” means mature intellect and judgment, generally reached at forty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r14.anchor: و «الأشد» شدة البدن واستحكام أسره وقوته، واستوى معناه تكامل عقله وحزمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r15.claim: “Ḥukm” means wisdom; knowledge is familiarity with Abraham’s law, preparatory to Moses’s prophethood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p280/r15.anchor: و «الحكم» الحكمة، و «العلم» ، والمعرفة بشرع إبراهيم عليه السلام وهي مقدمة نبوته عليه السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

MAJAZ:v2p99/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r2.claim: Balagha ashuddahu means he reached maturity; ashudd is plural in sense and has no singular from the same word-form, according to the author.
MAJAZ:v2p99/r2.anchor: بلغ أي انتهى وموضع أشده موضع جميع ولا واحد له من لفظه

MAJAZ:v2p99/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī say the singular of ashudd is shadd, on the faʿl pattern, like baḥr and abḥur.
MAJAZ:v2p99/r3.anchor: قال الفراء والكسائي واحد الأشد شد على فعل وأفعل مثل بحر وأبحر

MAJAZ:v2p99/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r4.claim: Istawā means he became fully established and complete.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.claim: When Moses reached maturity and became settled, God gave him wisdom and knowledge; this is how God rewards those who do good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.anchor: لما بلغ أشده واستوى، آتاه الله حكما وعلما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the wisdom and knowledge given to Moses as prophethood.

JISHUMI:v8p5478/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r2.claim: Ashudd means strength and bodily vigor; it is a plural of shidda, like niʿma and anʿum.
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r2.anchor: الأشد: جمع شدة، مثل نعمة وأنعم، وهي القوة والجلادة في البدن

JISHUMI:v8p5478/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r3.claim: Ashudd may refer to ages fifteen through forty.
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r3.anchor: وقيل: الأشد في خمسة عشر إلى أربعين سنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r1.claim: استوى means Moses became mature, fully settled and complete, reaching an age beyond further increase; al-Laqīṭ's cited line illustrates this completion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r1.anchor: واعتدل وتم استحكامه ، وبلغ المبلغ الذي لا يزاد عليه ، كما قال لقيط : واستحملوا أمركم لله دركمو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r2.claim: Moses reached this maturity at forty years.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r2.anchor: وذلك أربعون سنة ، ويروى : ( 810 ) أنه لم يبعث نبي إلا على رأس أربعين سنة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r3.claim: A report says that no prophet was commissioned before reaching forty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r3.anchor: ويروى : ( 810 ) أنه لم يبعث نبي إلا على رأس أربعين سنة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r4.claim: Here العلم means the Torah, and الحكم means the Sunna; the wisdom of prophets is their Sunna.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r4.anchor: العلم . التوراة . والحكم : السنة . وحكمة الأنبياء : سنتهم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r5.claim: Alternatively, God gave Moses the conduct and bearing of wise, learned men before prophethood, so he did nothing foolish.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p402/r5.anchor: وقيل : معناه أتيناه سيرة الحكماء العلماء ، وسمتهم قبل البعث ، فكان لا يفعل فعلا يستجهل فيه .

NAHHAS:v3p231/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r1.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p231/r1.claim: Sībawayh treats ashudd as the plural of shidda; another view makes it the plural of shadd, while a third treats it as a singular noun.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r1.anchor: عند سيبويه جمع شدة وقال غيره هو جميع شد وقيل هو واحد

NAHHAS:v3p231/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p231/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq says ashadd is not the only Arabic singular on the afʿal pattern without tāʾ, since linguists record aṣbaʿ; al-Naḥḥās calls his denial a mistake.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r2.anchor: أنه لا يعرف في كلام العرب اسم واحد على أفعل بغير هاء إلا أشد وهو وهم وقد حكى أهل اللغة أصبع

NAHHAS:v3p231/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p231/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and other exegetes take ‘he reached his full strength’ to mean that Moses reached forty years of age.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r3.anchor: ( واستوى ) أهل التفسير منهم ابن عباس على أن معنى واستوى بلغ أربعين سنة

NAHHAS:v3p231/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p231/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows the literal sense: ‘he reached his full strength’ describes attaining maturity.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r4.anchor: وتأوله أبو إسحاق على أنه يجوز أن يكون حقيقة واستوى وصف بلوغ الأشد

NAHHAS:v3p231/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p231/r5.claim: A wise and knowledgeable person is one who acts according to his knowledge.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r5.anchor: العالم والحكيم هو الذي يعمل بعلمه

NAHHAS:v3p231/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p231/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p231/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq says that granting wisdom and knowledge is presented as a reward for excellence because they lead to Paradise, the reward of the excellent.
NAHHAS:v3p231/r6.anchor: فجعل إتيان العلم والحكمة جزاء الإحسان لأنهما يؤديان إلى الجنة التي هي جزاء المحسنين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Moses reached maturity at forty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r2.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r2.claim: Sufyān says Moses reached maturity at thirty-four.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r2.anchor: الثاني : أربع وثلاثون سنة , قاله سفيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the age was thirty-three.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r3.anchor: الثالث : ثلاث وثلاثون سنة , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the age was thirty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r5.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says the age was twenty-five.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r5.anchor: الخامس : خمس وعشرون سنة , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r6.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām says the age was twenty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r6.anchor: السادس : عشرون سنة , حكاه يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the age was eighteen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r7.anchor: السابع : ثماني عشرة سنة , قاله ابن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r8.speaker: محمد بن قيس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r8.claim: Muḥammad ibn Qays says the age was fifteen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r8.anchor: الثامن : خمس عشرة سنة , قاله محمد بن قيس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r9.speaker: ربيعة ومالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r9.claim: Rabīʿa and Mālik say “maturity” means puberty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says al-ashudd is a plural without a singular.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r10.anchor: أحدهما : لا واحد له , قاله أبو عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r11.speaker: سيبويه
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r11.claim: Sībawayh says the singular of al-ashudd is shadd.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r12.speaker: الكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r12.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says its singular is shidda.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r13.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r13.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets istawā as bodily strength becoming balanced.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r13.anchor: أحدها : اعتدال القوة , قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r14.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r14.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets istawā as the growth of a beard.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r14.anchor: الثاني : خروج اللحية , قاله ابن قتيبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba also interprets istawā as the completion of youth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r15.anchor: الثالث : انتهى شبابه , قاله ابن قتيبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says istawā refers to forty years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r16.anchor: الرابع : أربعون سنة , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r20.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p240/r20.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says ḥukm means understanding of religion.

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r1.claim: Moses reached full strength at eighteen and maturity at forty; God then gave him knowledge and understanding.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r1.anchor: موسى { أشده } يعني لثماني عشرة سنة، { واستوى } يعني أربعين سنة، { آتيناه حكما وعلما }

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r2.claim: God rewards benefactors in this way, meaning those who believe in God.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r2.anchor: يقول: هكذا نجزي من أحسن، يعني من آمن بالله عز وجل،

MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.claim: Moses was at a village called Khanin, two farsakhs away, and came to the town at midday.
MUQATIL:28:14-15/r3.anchor: وكان بقرية تدعى خانين على رأس فرسخين، فأتى المدينة فدخلها نصف النهار.

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r1.claim: One interpretation makes the bestowal prophethood with its accompanying sciences and virtues; the connective waw does not establish whether it came before or after the killing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r1.anchor: أنها النبوة وما يقرن بها من العلوم والأخلاق

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.claim: The waw in ‘and he entered the city’ does not establish sequence, so this reading cannot date Moses’ prophethood relative to the killing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r2.anchor: لأن الواو في قوله : { ودخل المدينة } لا تفيد الترتيب

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r3.claim: Rāzī prefers interpreting ḥukm and knowledge as wisdom and learning, citing the Qur’anic pairing of wisdom with revelation in the homes.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r3.anchor: آتيناه الحكمة والعلم قال تعالى : { واذكرن ما يتلى فى بيوتكن من ءايات الله والحكمة } ( الأحزاب : 34 )

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r4.claim: Prophethood is the highest human rank and must follow completeness in knowledge and upright character, supporting the wisdom-and-learning interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r4.anchor: أن النبوة أعلى الدرجات البشرية فلا بد وأن تكون مسبوقة بالكمال في العلم والسيرة المرضية

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r5.claim: The phrase about rewarding the excellent implies that wisdom and knowledge were recompense for good conduct; prophethood is not a recompense for deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r5.anchor: قوله : { وكذلك نجزى المحسنين } يدل على أنه إنما أعطاه الحكم والعلم مجازاة على إحسانه والنبوة لا تكون جزاء على العمل

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r6.claim: If ḥukm and knowledge meant prophethood, the statement that the excellent are rewarded this way would imply that every excellent person becomes a prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r6.anchor: المراد بالحكم والعلم لو كان هو النبوة ، لوجب حصول النبوة لكل من كان من المحسنين

RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.claim: The passage indicates that God favored Moses with wisdom and knowledge before the killing of the Copt.
RAZI-FULL:v24p199/r7.anchor: ثم بين إنعامه عليه قبل قتل القبطي

TABRISI:28:12-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:12-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:12-15/r6.claim: Moses reached full strength at thirty-three years and maturity at forty.
TABRISI:28:12-15/r6.anchor: سنة { واستوى } أي بلغ أربعين سنة

TABRISI:28:12-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:12-15/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس
TABRISI:28:12-15/r7.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Ibn ʿAbbās say Moses' maturity occurred at forty.
TABRISI:28:12-15/r7.anchor: واستوى } أي بلغ أربعين سنة عن مجاهد وقتادة وابن عباس

TABRISI:28:12-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:12-15/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:12-15/r8.claim: God gave Moses understanding, knowledge, and reason in his own and his forefathers' religion; Moses had judgment and knowledge before becoming a prophet.
TABRISI:28:12-15/r8.anchor: أي فقها وعلما وعقلا بدينه ودين آبائه فعلم موسى وحكم قبل أن يبعث نبيا.

TABRISI:28:12-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:12-15/r9.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:28:12-15/r9.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the gift as prophethood and knowledge.

TABRISI:28:12-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:12-15/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:12-15/r10.claim: The statement that God rewards benefactors is explained in Sūrat Yūsuf.
TABRISI:28:12-15/r10.anchor: وكذلك نجزي المحسنين } وهذه الآية مفسرة في سورة يوسف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:11-15/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:11-15/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:11-15/r4.claim: Moses reached full strength above thirty and maturity at forty; God gave him reason, understanding, and knowledge before prophethood.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:11-15/r4.anchor: استوى } وبلغ أربعين سنة { آتيناه حكما } عقلا وفهما { وعلما } قبل النبوة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddī places Moses's reaching full strength at age twenty.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says Moses reached full strength at twenty and reached maturity at forty.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r2.anchor: تفسير مجاهد: {بلغ أشده} [القصص: 14] عشرين سنة {واستوى} [القصص: 14] بلغ أربعين سنة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r3.claim: “We gave him” means God granted him; the understanding and intelligence given to Moses are glossed by al-Suddī.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p581#2/r3.anchor: {آتيناه} [القصص: 14] أعطيناه. {حكما وعلما} [القصص: 14] ، يعني: فهما وعقلا، وهو تفسير السدي.

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r2.claim: One view puts Moses' reaching full strength at roughly thirty-three to thirty-nine years of age.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r2.anchor: قيل الأشد بضع وثلاثون سنة. وهو ما بين ثلاث وثلاثين إلى تسع وثلاثين.

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r3.claim: More generally, reaching full strength means completing a man's utmost physical vigor.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r3.anchor: وتأويل (بلغ أشده) استكمل نهاية قوة الرجل

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r4.claim: One view interprets استوى as reaching forty years.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r4.anchor: وقيل إن معنى واستوى - بلغ الأربعين.

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r5.claim: Alternatively, استوى can mean that he attained full maturity.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r5.anchor: وجائز أن يكون " استوى " وصل حقيقة بلوغ الأشد.

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r6.claim: Moses was given wisdom and knowledge before he was commissioned as a messenger.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r6.anchor: فعلم موسى عليه السلام وحكم قبل أن يبعث.

ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r7.claim: Knowledge and wisdom reward good conduct because they lead to Paradise; a learned person must act on knowledge, since those who did not act are called ignorant.
ZAJJAJ:v4p135/r7.anchor: فجعل الله إتيان العلم والحكمة مجازاة على الإحسان لأنهما يؤديان إلى الجنة التي هي جزاء المحسنين

ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r1.claim: The verse combines God's blessing of deep spiritual consciousness (ilm) with rational judgment (hukm), the ability to distinguish right from wrong.
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r1.anchor: stresses the supreme divine blessing of spiritual consciousness ('ilm in its deepest significance) combined with rational thought, as expressed in the concept of hukm

ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r2.claim: Asad notes that nearly the same statement about Joseph appears at 12:22.
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r2.anchor: This statement, almost entirely identical with 12:22

ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r3.claim: Moses reached this spiritual maturity after the events of verses 15 onward, as indicated by 26:20.
ASAD-NOTES:28:14#n12/r3.anchor: Moses reached this spiritual maturity after the events described in verses 15 ff.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r1.claim: Qatada says Moses reached full maturity at forty.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولما بلغ أشده واستوى ﴾ قال استوى بلغ أربعين سنة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r2.claim: Mujahid also says that Moses reached full maturity at forty.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن خثيم عن مجاهد قال استوى أربعين سنة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r3.claim: Qatada separately says Moses reached his ashudd, or full strength, at thirty-three.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p88#4/r3.anchor: وقال معمر وقال قتادة أشده ثلاث وثلاثون سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r1.claim: Reaching full strength means reaching the point beyond which a person's growth does not increase.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r1.anchor: أي المبلغ الذي لايزيد عليه نشؤه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r2.claim: Istiwāʾ means becoming complete and mature, reinforcing and explaining the preceding phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r2.anchor: أي كمل وتم تأكيد وتفسير لما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r3.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ sets full strength at ages eighteen to thirty and maturity at thirty to forty, after which decline begins.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r3.anchor: من طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس أنه قال الاشد ما بين الثماني عشر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r4.claim: Mujāhid sets full strength at thirty-three and maturity at forty; the same is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās and similarly from Qatāda.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال الاشد ثلاث وثلاثون سنة والاستواء اربعون سنة وهي رواية عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj once defines full strength as beginning around seventeen and extending to forty.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج مرة بلوغ الاشد من نحو سبع عشرة سنة إلى الاربعين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj also gives the range of thirty to forty for full strength.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r6.anchor: واخرى هو ما بين الثلاثين إلى الاربعين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r7.claim: Some prefer the thirty-to-forty range because 46:15 couples reaching full strength with reaching forty; al-Ālūsī says this inference is not free of difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r7.anchor: واختاره بعضهم هنا وعلل بأن ذلك لموافقته قوله تعالى : ( حتى إدا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the general sense: full strength is reaching the limit of bodily power and growth, while maturity is mental balance and perfection; timing varies by region, era, and circumstance.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r8.anchor: والحق أن بلوغ الاشد في الاصل هو الانتهاء إلى حد القوة وذلك وقت انتهاء النمو

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r9.claim: Moses's bodily strength and mental maturity should not be assigned a precise age without a reliable report, although forty is commonly said to be the usual age.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r9.anchor: ولا ينبغي تعيين وقت لذلك في حق موسى عليه السلام إلا بخبر يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r10.claim: A cited poem treats forty as the usual threshold of maturity, and 46:15 offers a supporting parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r10.anchor: نعم اشتهر أن ذلك في الأغلب يكون في سن اربعين وعليه قول الشاعر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r11.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r11.claim: Al-Suddī explains the judgment bestowed on Moses as prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r11.anchor: أي نبوة على ما وري عن السدي أو علما هو من خواص النبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r12.claim: Others interpret the gift as knowledge belonging to the special qualities of prophethood, or as knowledge of religion and sacred law.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r12.anchor: أو علما هو من خواص النبوة على ما تأول به بعضهم كلامه وعلما بالدين والشريعة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says knowledge means the Torah and judgment means the Sunnah, the practice of the prophets; the verse about what is recited in the houses of the Prophet's wives joins Scripture and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r13.anchor: وفي الكشاف العلم التوراة والحكم السنة وحكمة الانبياء عليهم السلام سنتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r14.claim: Another view is that before his mission Moses received the conduct and bearing of wise, learned people and never acted foolishly.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r14.anchor: وقيل آتيناه سيرة الحكماء العلماى وسمتهم قبل البعث فكان عليه السلام لايفعل فعلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors the pre-mission conduct-and-knowledge interpretation as it better fits the narrative sequence: Moses's commissioning followed the killing, migration to Midian, return, and Pharaoh's drowning.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p51/r15.anchor: ورجح ما قيل بأنه أوفق لنظم القصة مما تقدم لأن استنباءه عليه السلام بعد وكز القبطي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r1.claim: Reading the earlier gift as prophethood sits uneasily with the statement that benefactors are rewarded, since prophethood is not a reward for deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r1.anchor: على إحسانهم يأبى جمل ما تقدم على النبوة لأنها لا تكون جزاء على العمل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r2.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r2.claim: Those who take the gift as prophethood regard it as a summary of the promise to make Moses a messenger after his return to his mother, with later verses detailing it; the conjunction wāw does not require chronological order.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r2.anchor: ومن ذهب إلدى الأول جعل هذا بيانا اجماليا لانجاز الوعد بجعله من المرسلين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r3.speaker: أصحاب القول الأول
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r3.claim: On the prophethood reading, what God did for Moses and his mother counts as recompense by a generalizing attribution, and prophethood's higher degrees of nearness may reward righteous action.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r3.anchor: وكون ما فعل بموسى وأمه عليهما السلام جزاء على العمل باعتبار التغليب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r4.claim: Prophethood itself is not earned as a reward, but a degree of it involving increased nearness to God can be recompense; prophets differ in their nearness to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r4.anchor: أصل النبوة وإن لم تكن جزاء على العمل إلا أن بعض مراتبها وهو ما فيه ميد قرب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī further prefers the non-prophethood interpretation because it better suits the promise that Moses's mother would know God's promise true; the implication that every benefactor receives prophethood is no objection to that reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r6.speaker: من ذهب إلى أن الإيتاء كان قبل الهجرة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r6.claim: If the gift came before migration, it could mean leadership among the Israelites, who turned to Moses in important matters and obeyed his commands, together with useful knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r6.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أن الايتاء كان قبل الهجرة قال : يجوز أن يكون المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r7.speaker: من ذهب إلى أن الإيتاء كان قبل الهجرة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r7.claim: This knowledge could come through inspiration or Moses's insight into teachings transmitted from his prophetic ancestors; he could know their beliefs and laws by inspiration or reliable reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r7.anchor: وذلك إما بمحض الإلهام أو بتوفيقه لاستنباط دقائق وأسرار مما نقل اليه من كلمات آبائه الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī considers the pre-migration leadership-and-knowledge explanation perhaps preferable to the report quoted in al-Kashshāf and points readers to his discussion near the end of al-Baqara.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p52/r8.anchor: ولعل هذا أولى مما نقله في الكشاف وفي الكلام على أواخر سورة البقرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi defines Moses’ reaching full strength as ages eighteen through thirty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: الأشد ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين سنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and others say full strength came at thirty-three and istawa means reaching forty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r3.anchor: [قال مجاهد وغيره: ثلاث وثلاثون سنة، {واستوى} أي: بلغ أربعين سنة]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr transmits this age explanation from Ibn ʿAbbas.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r4.anchor: ورواه (2) سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r5.claim: An alternative gloss of istawa is that Moses had reached the end of youth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r6.claim: God gave Moses jurisprudence, reason, and religious knowledge; he was taught and exercised judgment before prophethood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p195#2/r6.anchor: أي: الفقه والعقل والعلم في الدين، فعلم موسى وحكم قبل أن يبعث نبيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r3.claim: Ashudd is full development, beyond which growth does not increase; this is placed at thirty to forty when reason matures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r3.anchor: مبلغه الذي لا يزيد عليه نشؤه وذلك من ثلاثين إلى أربعين سنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r4.claim: A report says every prophet was commissioned at forty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r4.anchor: وروي أنه لم يبعث نبي إلا على رأس الأربعين سنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r5.claim: Istawā may refer to Moses' stature or intellect.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r6.claim: Ḥukm means prophethood, while ʿilm means knowledge of religion.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r7.claim: Alternatively, God gave him the bearing and knowledge of scholars before prophethood, so he would not act foolishly; this better fits the narrative order.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r7.anchor: أو علم الحكماء والعلماء وسمتهم قبل استنبائه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r8.claim: God rewards benefactors as He rewarded Moses and his mother.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:13-14/r8.anchor: مثل ذلك الذي فعلنا بموسى وأمه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r9.claim: Ashudd refers to the completion of Moses’s strengths and capacities.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r9.anchor: { ولما بلغ أشده } أي مجامع قواه وكمالاته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r10.claim: Istiwāʾ means reaching mature, settled adulthood after youth is complete, which Biqāʿī places between ages twenty-one and forty-two.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r10.anchor: { واستوى } أي اعتدل في السن وتم استحكامه بانتهاء الشباب , وهو من العمر ما بين إحدى وعشرين سنة إلى اثنين وأربعين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r11.speaker: الجنيد
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r11.claim: Al-Junayd says this is when intellect is complete, insight sound, and character excellent, so the time for receiving the divine address has arrived.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r11.anchor: وقال الرازي : قال الجنيد : لما تكامل عقله , وصحت بصيرته , وصلحت نحيرته , وآن أوان خطابه أنتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r12.claim: God chose Moses’s age for his mission as a sign: ordinary people stop gaining new faculties after youth and then decline, as 36:68 states.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r12.anchor: واختار الله سبحانه هذا السن للإرسال ليكون - كما أشير إليه - من جملة الخوارقن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r13.claim: Unlike ordinary people, prophets and righteous followers whom God singles out can grow in knowledge and bodily strength at the age when others decline, without acquisition.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r13.anchor: هذه عادة الله في جميع بني آدم إلا الأنبياء , فإنهم في حد الوقوف يؤتون من بحار العلوم ما يقصر عنه الوصف بغير اكتساب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r14.claim: God’s gift of wisdom and knowledge is miraculous and innate, not acquired by Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r14.anchor: { آتيناه } اي خرقا للعادة أسوة إخوانه من الأنبياء ابتداء غرائز منحناه إياها من غير اكتساب أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r15.claim: Wisdom is action perfected through knowledge, and knowledge is supported by wisdom; these gifts prepare Moses for prophethood and anticipate his mission.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r15.anchor: { حكما } أي عملا محكما بالعلم { وعلما } اي مؤيدا بالحكمة , تهيئة لنبوته , وإرهاصا لرسالته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r16.claim: God rewarded Moses and his mother for sincere goodness and reliance on Him alone; the promise generalizes to all who do good.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p469#2/r16.anchor: فعلنا به ذلك وبأمه جزاء لهما على إحسانهما في إخلاصهما فيما يفعلانه اعتمادا على وحده من غير أدنى التفات

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r3.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās, transmitted through Mujāhid, places Moses’ reaching full strength at age thirty-three.
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r3.anchor: عن طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ولما بلغ أشده} قال: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r4.claim: In the same report, Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses reached maturity at age forty.

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r5.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās defines full strength as ages eighteen to thirty and maturity as thirty to forty, after which decline begins.
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ولما بلغ أشده واستوى} قال: الاشد ما بين الثماني عشرة إلى الثلاثين

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r6.claim: Mujāhid explains ḥukm as judgment, understanding, and intellect, and knowledge as prophethood.
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولما بلغ أشده} قال: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة {واستوى} قال: أربعين سنة {آتيناه حكما وعلما} قال: الحكم والفقه والعقل والعلم قال: النبوة

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r7.speaker: أبو قبيصة
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r7.claim: Abū Qubayṣa interprets Moses’ maturity as the growth of his beard.
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r7.anchor: عن أبي قبيصة رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: يعني بالاستواء: خروج لحيته

DURR-FULL:v6p396/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r8.claim: Qatāda, like one report from Ibn ʿAbbās, places full strength at thirty-three and maturity at forty.
DURR-FULL:v6p396/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {ولما بلغ أشده} قال: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة {واستوى} قال: أربعين سنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r1.speaker: ربيعة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r1.claim: Rabīʿa says reaching maturity means reaching puberty.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r1.anchor: عن ربيعة في قول الله : بلغ اشده اشده : الحلم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam is reported by his son to give the same gloss, puberty.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r2.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم ، عن أبيه مثله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r3.claim: Mālik is also reported to give the same gloss of reaching maturity as puberty.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r3.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم ، عن أبيه مثله . قال مالك : مثله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r4.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī dates the reaching of full strength to age thirty-four.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r4.anchor: قال : سمعت سفيان الثوري يقول : بلغ اشده إلى اربعة وثلاثين سنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses reached full maturity at forty.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس واستوى قال : اربعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r6.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، زيد بن اسلم، الثوري
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r6.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, Zayd ibn Aslam, and al-Thawrī are each reported to identify full maturity as age forty.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r6.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد وقتادة وزيد بن اسلم والثوري مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r7.speaker: ابن قبيصة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r7.claim: Ibn Qubayṣa explains full maturity and settling as the growth of Moses' beard.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r7.anchor: عن ابن قبيصة في قوله : بلغ اشده واستوى يعني بالاستواء : خروج لحيته

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r8.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r8.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says God granted Moses judgment and knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r8.anchor: عن محمد ابن اسحاق ولما بلغ اشده واستوى اتيناه حكما وعلما اي اتاه الله حكما وعلما

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r9.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r9.anchor: عن اسماعيل بن مسلم ، عن عكرمة قال : الحكم اللب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses judgment as knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس قال : الحكم : العلم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r11.claim: Mujahid says Moses received understanding of religion, sound judgment, and knowledge before prophethood.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r11.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد قوله : اتيناه حكما وعلما قال : الفقه والعقل والعلم قبل النبوة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r12.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r12.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r12.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the judgment and knowledge granted to Moses as prophethood.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r12.anchor: عن السدي قوله : اتيناه حكما وعلما قال : النبوة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r13.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r13.claim: Mujahid gives another gloss of judgment: the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2951/r13.anchor: عن سفيان ، عن رجل ، عن مجاهد : الحكم قال : هو القران

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r1.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains Moses' knowledge as understanding his religion and that of his forefathers, including its laws and limits.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r1.anchor: محمد بن اسحاق اتيناه حكما وعلما اي اتاه الله حكما وعلما ، فقها في دينه ودين ابائه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r2.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq connects Moses' gift of judgment and knowledge with God's stated reward of those who do good.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2952/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، قال : ولما بلغ اشده واستوى اتيناه حكما وعلما اتاه الله حكما وعلما يقول الله : وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r2.claim: Verse 14 is an interlude within the story’s chronology, prompted by the promise to Moses’s mother; that promise was fulfilled when the narrative completed his return to her in verse 13.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r2.anchor: هذا اعتراض بين أجزاء القصة المرتبة على حسب ظهورها في الخارج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r3.claim: Moses received prophethood only after leaving Midian, as the later account says when he completed the term and set out with his family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r3.anchor: وإنما أوتي الحكم أعني النبوءة بعد خروجه من أرض مدين كما سيجيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r4.claim: A parallel to this verse appears in Sūrat Yūsuf, though that verse lacks the additional description ‘and he became fully formed.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r4.anchor: وتقدم نظير هذه الآية في سورة يوسف ، إلا قوله { واستوى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r5.claim: Some take istawā as a synonym of reaching full strength and therefore an emphasis; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects this, taking ashudd as full strength and istiwāʾ as bodily completeness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r5.anchor: و الحق أن الأشد كمال القوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r6.claim: Istiwāʾ means bodily completeness, as when crops thicken and stand upright; Moses is described this way, unlike Joseph, because Moses was tall and fully built.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r6.anchor: وأن الاستواء : كمال البنية كقوله تعالى في وصف الزرع { فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r7.claim: A Prophetic description says Moses was like one of the men of Shanūʾa; his full build helps explain why his blow killed the Egyptian.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r7.anchor: كما في الحديث ( كأنه من رجال شنؤة ) فكان كامل الأعضاء ولذلك كان وكزه القبطي قاضيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p87/r8.claim: Here ḥukm means wisdom, while ʿilm means knowledge of God.

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r1.claim: Ashudd means strength, here the period from eighteen to thirty; the singular form is built on a plural pattern.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r1.anchor: أي : قوته وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين واحد على بناء الجميع

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r2.claim: Istiwāʾ means becoming balanced and mature in intellect; Moses reached this maturity at forty, as 46:15 indicates.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r2.anchor: والاستواء اعتدال الشيء في ذاته أي اعتدل عقله وكمل بأن بلغ أربيعين سنة

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r3.claim: Yusuf's account says only that he reached full strength because he received revelation in youth while in the well; Moses received revelation after forty.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r3.anchor: وفي يوسف {بلغ أشده} (يوسف : 22) فحسب لأنه أوحى إليه في صباه حين كونه في البئر

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r4.claim: The gift of judgment means prophethood, while knowledge means knowledge of religion.

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi says the account mentions the announcement of prophethood and that God made Moses a prophet after the migration, on his return from Midian to Egypt.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ذكر انباي نبوت دراثناي اين قضيه) أي معه أنه تعالى استنبأه

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r6.speaker: الجمهور
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r6.claim: The majority holds that Muhammad was commissioned at forty; some extend the same age to every prophet.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أن نبينا عليه السلام بعث على رأس الأربعين وكذا كل نبي عند البعض

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r7.claim: Others reject forty as a required age for prophets, citing Jesus at thirty-three, Joseph at eighteen, and John at two or three; Sahl al-Tustari attained spiritual knowledge before puberty.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اشتراط الأربعين في حق الأنبياء ليس بشيء لأن عيسى عليه السلام نبىء ورفع إلى السماء وهو ابن ثلاث وثلاثين

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r8.claim: Divine gifts reach a servant when their time comes, however long the delay; seekers should await God's favor without despair, since He rewards those who do good.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r8.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على أن العطية الإلهية تصل إلى العبد وإن طال العهد إذا جاء أوانها

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r9.claim: Moses and his mother were doers of good and pious in their early years; God rewards anyone who joins their company with the best recompense.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r9.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أنهما كانا محسنين في عملهما متقيين في عنفوان عمرهما

BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r10.claim: A woman gave a beggar a bite, then a wolf snatched her child; after her prayer, a rescuer pulled the child unharmed from the wolf's mouth, repaying her charity.
BURSEVI:v6p282#3/r10.anchor: حكي : أن امرأة كانت تتعشى فسألها سائل فقامت ووضعت في فمه لقمة ثم وضعت ولدها في موضع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r1.claim: The commentary points back to the discussion in Joseph and says commentators' explanations are similar, though they distinguish reaching maturity from attaining full strength; the maturity term was discussed in al-Anʿam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r1.anchor: قد فسرنا هذه الآية في سورة يوسف وكلام المفسرين في لفظ الآيتين متقارب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say Moses reached full maturity at forty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه أربعون سنة قاله مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد والثاني ستون سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir gives sixty years as the age at which Moses reached full maturity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r3.anchor: والثاني ستون سنة ذكره ابن جرير قال المفسرون مكث عند أمه حتى فطمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r4.claim: The commentators say Moses stayed with his mother until weaning, then grew up in Pharaoh and his wife's household, where they adopted him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p207/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون مكث عند أمه حتى فطمته ثم ردته إليهم فنشأ في حجر فرعون وامرأته

MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r1.claim: Moses reached his full strength at thirty-three years of age.
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولما بلغ أشده ﴾ يعني ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r2.claim: Moses reached maturity at forty years of age.

MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r3.claim: The wisdom and knowledge given to Moses mean understanding, intelligence, and knowledge, bestowed before prophethood.
MUJAHID:v2p481#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ آتيناه حكما وعلما ﴾ قال يعني الفقه والعقل والعلم ( 2 ) قبل النبوة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r1.claim: Moses reached full strength and maturity of intellect; ashudd is a plural of shidda in Sibawayh's analysis, like niʿma and anʿum.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r1.anchor: بلغ موسى نهاية القوة وتمام العقل وهو جمع شدة كنعمة وأنعم عند سيبويه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r2.claim: Istawa means he became balanced and fully mature; this was at forty.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r2.anchor: واعتدل وتم استحكامه وهو أربعون سنة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r3.claim: A report says no prophet was commissioned before reaching forty.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r3.anchor: ويروى أنه لم يبعث نبي إلا على رأس أربعين سنة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r4.claim: God gave Moses prophethood as wisdom and either jurisprudence or knowledge of the interests of both worlds.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r5.claim: As God treated Moses and his mother, He treats believers; knowledge and wisdom are recompense because they lead to Paradise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r5.anchor: كما فعلنا بموسى وأمه نفعل بالمؤمنين قال الزجاج جعل الله تعالى ايتاء العلم والحكمة مجازاة على الإحسان لأنهما يؤديان إلى الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r6.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the truly learned and wise act on their knowledge; scripture calls those who do not so ignorant.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p229#4/r6.anchor: والعالم الحكيم من يعمل بعلمه لأنه تعالى قال ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لوكانوا يعلمون فجعلهم جهالا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:12-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:12-14/r14.speaker: ربيعة ومالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:12-14/r14.claim: Rabiʿa and Mālik say al-ashudd means puberty; Qurṭubī prefers this, supported by the age of marriage in 4:6.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:12-14/r14.anchor: وقول ربيعة ومالك أنه الحلم أولى ما قيل فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r1.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r1.claim: The cited phrase marks the beginning of al-ashudd, and Sufyān al-Thawrī sets its farthest limit at age thirty-four.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r1.anchor: فإن ذلك أول الأشد، وأقصاه أربع وثلاثون سنة وهو قول سفيان الثوري.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says istawā means Moses reached age forty.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r2.anchor: و { استوى } قال ابن عباس: بلغ أربعين سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r3.claim: One explanation takes ḥukm as wisdom before prophethood; another takes it as understanding of religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r3.anchor: والحكم: الحكمة قبل النبوة. وقيل: الفقه في الدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r5.claim: Another view understands the knowledge given to Moses as prophethood.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the gift as jurisprudence or understanding.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r7.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses knew his religion and that of his forefathers; before prophethood, nine Israelites listened to him, followed him, and gathered around him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r7.anchor: محمد ابن إسحاق: أي العلم بما في دينه ودين آبائه وكان له تسعة من بني إسرائيل يسمعون منه، ويقتدون به، ويجتمعون إليه، وكان هذا قبل النبوة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r8.claim: As God rewarded Moses' mother for submitting, placing her child in the river, and trusting His promise, so He rewards every good-doer; He returned her child safely and later gave Moses reason, wisdom, and prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:14/r8.anchor: أي كما جزينا أم موسى لما استسلمت لأمر الله، وألقت ولدها في البحر، وصدقت بوعد الله فرددنا ولدها إليها بالتحف والطرف وهي آمنة، ثم وهبنا له العقل والحكمة والنبوة وكذلك نجزي كل محسن.

QASHANI:28:13-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:13-14/r3.claim: Reaching maturity signifies the station of spiritual youth and perfected primordial nature; becoming established means attaining perfection and then detaching from the soul and its attributes.
QASHANI:28:13-14/r3.anchor: استقام بحصول كماله ثم بتجرده عن النفس وصفاته

QASHANI:28:13-14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:13-14/r4.claim: The wisdom and knowledge bestowed are theoretical and practical wisdom.
QASHANI:28:13-14/r4.anchor: آتيناه حكما وعلما } أي: حكمة نظرية وعملية

QASHANI:28:13-14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:13-14/r5.claim: The people rewarded as doers of good are those endowed with virtues and walking the path of justice.
QASHANI:28:13-14/r5.anchor: المحسنين } المتصفين بالفضائل، السائرين في طريق العدالة

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r1.claim: One view treats “reached full strength” and “became settled” as synonymous: full strength, balanced temperament, and mature constitution.
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنهما بمعنى واحد وهو استكمال القوة

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r2.claim: Rāzī calls it likelier that the terms differ: “full strength” is complete bodily power, while “settled” is complete intellectual power.
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r2.anchor: وهو الأقرب أن الأشد عبارة عن كمال القوة الجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r3.claim: A second distinction makes “full strength” complete power and “settled” the completion of bodily constitution and form.

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r4.claim: A third distinction takes “full strength” as reaching adulthood and “settled” as bodily perfection.

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās places full strength from age 18 to 30, a plateau from 30 to 40, then decline; Rāzī endorses this trajectory and explains that bodily powers wane as intellect grows, making forty fitting for prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس الأشد ما بين الثمان عشرة سنة إلى الثلاثين ثم من الثلاثين سنة إلى الأربعين يبقى سواء

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the singular of “ashudd” would analogically be “shadd,” though that singular is unattested.
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء : الأشد واحدها شد في القياس

RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r7.speaker: أبو الهيثم
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r7.claim: Abū al-Haytham gives “shidda” as the singular, paralleling “niʿma” as the singular of “anʿām”; shidda means strength and toughness.
RAZI-FULL:v24p198#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم : واحد الأشد شدة

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r1.claim: The verse's maturity language is linked to Joseph's maturity and to the age when orphans become independent; Islamic law's various maturity ages are discussed at 4:6c.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r1.anchor: 12:22, which speaks of wisdom and knowledge being given to Joseph at the time of his maturity

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r2.claim: Istawā can mean to mount, turn or direct oneself, or be equal or the same.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r2.anchor: a rich range of meaning, including “to mount”

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r3.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r3.claim: The word implies adult balance and sure footing; inwardly, this means balance between hope and fear, humility and dignity, and dependence and autonomy, when true wisdom begins.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r3.anchor: it implies the stage at which one achieves the balance and sure footing of adulthood

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r4.claim: As a physical description, being firmly established is thought to refer to age forty, the traditional age of prophethood and Muhammad's first revelation.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r4.anchor: it is thought to refer to the age of forty (the age of prophethood, as it is commonly known in Muslim tradition, and the age at which Muhammad first received the revelation; Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r5.claim: Some treat reaching maturity and being firmly established as synonymous.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r5.anchor: Some treat these two ideas as synonymous

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r6.claim: R distinguishes physical maturity, often the end of puberty, from intellectual and psychological maturity around forty.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r6.anchor: often associated with the end of puberty and the second with reaching the age of forty (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r7.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r7.claim: Ṭ gives the ages as thirty-three and forty, respectively.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r7.anchor: they refer to thirty-three and forty years old, respectively (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r8.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r8.claim: Ṭ understands wisdom as prophetic wisdom before investiture, and knowledge as understanding religious matters.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r8.anchor: wisdom that is possessed by a prophet before his investiture with prophethood, while knowledge refers to understanding in religious matters (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r9.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r9.claim: Q understands knowledge here as knowledge of the religious tradition of Moses' Israelite forefathers.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r9.anchor: knowledge in the religious tradition of Moses’ forefathers among the Israelites (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r10.speaker: M
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r10.claim: M says wisdom here means the ability to judge between people.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r10.anchor: the wisdom to judge between people (M)

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r11.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r11.claim: Q reads God's recompense of the virtuous as His rewarding and blessing Moses' mother: giving her a son, returning him after separation, and granting him sound judgment and intelligence.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r11.anchor: how God rewarded and blessed the mother of Moses by giving her a son, returning him to her after she was forced to relinquish him

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r12.claim: The recompense formula is linked with 6:84; 12:22; 37:80, 105, 110, 121, 131; 77:44; and 29:69c and 37:80c.

STUDYQURAN:28:14/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r13.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r13.claim: R reports the argument that the verse cannot mean prophethood, since Islamic tradition does not treat prophethood as a reward for merit.
STUDYQURAN:28:14/r13.anchor: this verse could not refer to prophethood, since according to the Islamic tradition prophethood is never given as a reward for merit (R)

TAB-FULL:v18p181/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p181/r1.claim: Moses reached the peak of bodily strength and powers; al-Ṭabarī says the word’s meaning and evidence were discussed earlier.
TAB-FULL:v18p181/r1.anchor: يعني حان شدة بدنه وقواه، وانتهى ذلك منه

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r1.claim: استوى means Moses completed his youth, his body and creation becoming fully formed and mature.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {ولما بلغ أشده} [القصص: 14] قال: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses reached his full strength at thirty-three and became fully mature at forty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {ولما بلغ أشده} [القصص: 14] قال: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة. قوله: {واستوى} [القصص: 14] قال: بلغ أربعين سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r3.claim: Mujahid also reports the view that full maturity comes at forty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r3.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {واستوى} [القصص: 14] قال: أربعين سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to place Moses’s reaching full strength at a few years past thirty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس،

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r5.claim: Qatada says full strength is thirty-three and full maturity is forty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، " {أشده واستوى} [القصص: 14] قال: أربعين سنة، وأشده: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd reports his father’s gloss: أشد means vigor, while full maturity occurs at forty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r6.anchor: كان أبي يقول: الأشد: الجلد، والاستواء: أربعون سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r7.claim: An unnamed view places the age of full maturity at thirty.
TAB-FULL:v18p181#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يكون ذلك في ثلاثين سنة

TAB-FULL:v18p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r1.claim: The wisdom granted to Moses means understanding of religion and knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {آتيناه حكما وعلما} [يوسف: 22] قال: الفقه، والعقل، والعمل قبل النبوة

TAB-FULL:v18p182/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the gift as religious learning, reason, and action before Moses’s prophethood.
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {آتيناه حكما وعلما} [يوسف: 22] قال: الفقه، والعقل، والعمل قبل النبوة

TAB-FULL:v18p182/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses received knowledge and understanding of his religion and his forefathers’ religion, including its rules and limits.
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {ولما بلغ أشده واستوى} [القصص: 14] آتاه الله حكما وعلما وفقها في دينه ودين آبائه، وعلما بما في دينه وشرائعه وحدوده

TAB-FULL:v18p182/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r4.claim: As God rewarded Moses for obedience, patience, and good conduct, He rewards every messenger and servant who obeys, endures, and avoids what He forbids.
TAB-FULL:v18p182/r4.anchor: كما جزينا موسى على طاعته إيانا وإحسانه بصبره على أمرنا، كذلك نجزي كل من أحسن من رسلنا وعبادنا

SULAMI:v2p101#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p101#4/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p101#4/r1.claim: When Moses’ intellect matured, insight became sound, and he was ready for address, God gave him judgment as clear understanding of himself and knowledge of new gifts arriving from his Lord.
SULAMI:v2p101#4/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه ، لما تكامل عقله وصحت بصيرته وحصلت نحيرته

TABATABAI:28:11-14/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:11-14/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:11-14/r10.claim: Reaching full strength usually occurs at eighteen; istiwāʾ means balance and stability, and in life means settled maturity, which varies among people but usually follows that age.
TABATABAI:28:11-14/r10.anchor: بلوغ الأشد أن يعمر الإنسان ما تشتد عند ذلك قواه ويكون في الغالب في الثمان عشرة

TABATABAI:28:14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:14/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:14/r3.claim: In a report from Imam al-Ṣādiq through Muḥammad b. al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal, reaching full strength means eighteen years and istiwāʾ means growing a beard.
TABATABAI:28:14/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن نعمان الأحول عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { فلما بلغ أشده واستوى } قال أشده ثمان عشرة سنة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r1.claim: The expression balagha ashuddahu was explained earlier.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r1.anchor: ولما بلغ أشده} قد تقدم ذكره (3) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r2.claim: Istawā means that his youth became complete and settled, with no further increase.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p329#3/r2.anchor: واستوى} أي استحكم وانتهى شبابه واستقر: فلم تكن فيه زيادة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r1.claim: Moses reached full strength between eighteen and forty years old.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني لثمان عشرة سنة إلى أربعين سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says Moses attained maturity at thirty-three.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r2.anchor: استوى وهو ابن ثلاث وثلاثين سنة. وهذا قول الكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid places full strength at thirty-three and full maturity at forty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ولما بلغ أشده: ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة، واستواؤه: أربعين سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda agree with Mujāhid's ages.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r5.claim: The wisdom and knowledge given to Moses were understanding, reason, and knowledge before prophethood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: الفقه والعقل والعلم قبل النبوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r6.claim: God gave Moses knowledge and understanding of his own religion, his fathers' religion, and its laws and limits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: آتاه الله علما وفقها في دينه، ودين آبائه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r7.claim: Moses had a following among the Children of Israel who listened to him, followed his example, and gathered around him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r7.anchor: وكانت له من بني إسرائيل شيعة يسمعون منه، ويقتدون به، ويجتمعون إليه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r8.claim: Moses possessed knowledge and wisdom before he was commissioned as a prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: فعلم موسى -عليه السلام- وحكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r9.claim: A learned wise person acts on knowledge; one who does not act on knowledge is ignorant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p350#2/r9.anchor: والعالم الحكيم من استعمل علمه، ومن لم يعمل بعلمه فهو جاهل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r1.claim: Here the excellent-doers are those who believe in God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول: هكذا نجزي من أحسن، أي: من آمن بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r2.claim: The excellent-doers are the people of monotheism.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r3.claim: God's gift of knowledge and wisdom rewards Moses for goodness because those gifts lead to Paradise, the reward of the excellent-doers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: جعل الله إيتاء العلم والحكمة إياه مجازاة على الإحسان؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r4.claim: The verse is explained further in Sūrat Yūsuf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p351/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية مفسرة في سورة يوسف

THALABI:v7p238/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p238/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v7p238/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi defines reaching full strength as ages eighteen through thirty.
THALABI:v7p238/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: الأشد: ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين سنة

THALABI:v7p238/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p238/r3.speaker: سائر المفسرين
THALABI:v7p238/r3.claim: Most commentators put full strength at thirty-three years and say istawā, “became established,” means forty years.
THALABI:v7p238/r3.anchor: وقال سائر المفسرين: الأشد ثلاث وثلاثون سنة، واستوى أي بلغ أربعين سنة.

THALABI:v7p238/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p238/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p238/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, gives thirty-three for full strength and forty for istiwāʾ, says Adam's descendants were allotted sixty years, and cites the verse about being given time to reflect.
THALABI:v7p238/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس في قول الله سبحانه: بلغ أشده واستوى قال: الأشد: ثلاث وثلاثون سنة

THALABI:v7p238/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p238/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p238/r5.claim: The wisdom given to Moses means reason, understanding, and knowledge.

THALABI:v7p238/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p238/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p238/r6.claim: Mujahid reports the interpretation that the wisdom bestowed on Moses was prophethood.
THALABI:v7p238/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: قيل: النبوة، وكذلك نجزي المحسنين.

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r12.claim: Istawā can mean to become strong and mature; the source explains the phrase as the completion of one's form at forty years.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r12.anchor: استوى بمعنى قوي واشتد قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r4.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r4.claim: Al-Hasan identifies Moses' reaching full strength with the time when proof and responsibility were complete.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r4.anchor: ولما بلغ أشده قيل: وقت تمام الحجة، عن الحسن.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r5.claim: Another explanation says signs of maturity appeared in Moses and he attained complete physical and mental strength.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r5.anchor: وقيل: أونس منه الرشد، وبلغ كمال قوته في البدن والعقل.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r6.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi places the age of full strength between eighteen and eighty.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r6.anchor: وقيل: الأشد: ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثمانين سنة، عن الكلبي.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada place full strength at sixty-three and his attaining full maturity at forty.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r7.anchor: وقيل: الأشد: ثلاث وستون سنة، واستواؤه أربعون سنة، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r8.claim: Istawā can mean reaching the end of intellect, becoming refined and sound; it can also mean completing bodily growth and proportion.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r8.anchor: واستوى بلغ نهاية العقل وتهذب وصلح، وقيل: استوى: بلغ تمام الخلق واعتدال الجسم

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r9.claim: One further view places this stage from age twenty-two until beyond forty.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r9.anchor: وقيل: يكون هذا في اثنتين وعشرين سنة إلى أن يجاوز أربعين سنة.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r10.claim: The gift of judgment and knowledge is explained as prophethood and knowledge, understanding and reason, or the disciplines of religious law.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r10.anchor: آتيناه أعطيناه حكما وعلما قيل: النبوة والعلم، وقيل: فهما وعقلا

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r11.claim: A third explanation identifies the gift as the sciences of religious law.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r12.claim: God sent Moses because his character qualified him for prophethood; the sending was not a reward earned by his deeds.
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r12.anchor: يعني: بعثناه لأنه كان بصفة تصلح للبعثة، لا أن البعث جزاء على العمل
